The tool loop is transparent to the client -- it does not need to track rounds.\n\nMessages a tool addresses to the client are forwarded verbatim, in the position the stream produced them, rather than being rewritten into entries of the server's own ([validated by: forwards a tool result to the client untouched](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L169)).\n\n## 10. Heartbeat\n\nTwo levels of heartbeat operate concurrently.\n\n### 10.1 WebSocket-Level Ping (Server-Initiated)\n\nThe server sends a WebSocket ping frame at the configured `heartbeatIntervalMs` interval (default 30 seconds). The client's WebSocket implementation responds automatically with a pong frame per RFC 6455 Section 5.5.3. If the server does not receive a pong within the interval, it MAY terminate the connection, which abandons the socket's turn like any close ([abandon-on-close](../hal-engine-abandon-on-close/spec.md)).\n\n### 10.2 Application-Level Ping (Client-Initiated)\n\nThe client SHOULD send a `ping` message (Section 4.2) every 5 seconds. The server responds with a `pong` message (Section 5.7). The client MAY use the round-trip time to display connection health indicators.\n\n## 11. Connection Termination\n\n### 11.1 Client Disconnect\n\nThe client SHOULD close the WebSocket with code 1000 (Normal Closure). The server keeps the session: it erases nothing on close, and the credentials the socket carried are cleared from it. Closing the socket abandons the turn it started: the run stops, no `stream_end` follows, and the session keeps the answer as it stood, committed and flagged `truncated` ([abandon-on-close](../hal-engine-abandon-on-close/spec.md)).\n\n### 11.2 Server Shutdown\n\n**Not implemented.** No signal handler is installed anywhere in the engine. `createServer` returns a `stop()` that closes every client socket with code 1001 and clears the heartbeat, but nothing wires it to `SIGTERM`, so today a terminating process drops connections abruptly. A host embedding the engine can call `stop()` from its own handler; making the engine do it is an open decision. Each socket `stop()` closes abandons its turn, so a deploy that stops the server abandons every turn in flight unless connections are drained first.\n\n### 11.3 Reconnection\n\nIf the connection drops unexpectedly, the client SHOULD reconnect using exponential backoff:\n\n- Base delay: 1,000 ms\n- Formula: `min(1000 * 2^retryCount + jitter, 31000)` where jitter is 0-1000 ms random\n- Maximum retries: 5\n- On reconnection success, any queued `user_message` messages MUST be flushed immediately.\n- On reconnection, the client MUST clear its local entries array and SHOULD send `?sessionId=` with the id from its last `connected` frame. When the server has resume enabled and the conversation is the user's own, it answers `resumed: true` and replays the conversation; otherwise the client is starting a new session.\n- An entry still streaming when its conversation is resumed is replayed with `isStreaming: false` and `truncated: true`: the rest of its turn streams to the connection that started it, so this one would wait for a commit that never comes ([validated by: replays an entry whose turn is still running as finished and truncated, leaving the stored entry as it is](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L364)).\n- With the server's `latest` option, a client that has lost the id, after a page refresh for instance, MAY connect without one and still rejoin its user's most recent conversation, and sends `?new=1` to start a new conversation instead ([validated by: with latest on, rejoins the most recently active session of a user whose connect names none](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L428), [validated by: with latest on, starts a new session for a user with none, and on ?new=1 even when one exists](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L445)).\n\nAfter 5 failed attempts, the client MUST stop reconnecting and report a disconnected state.\n\n## 12. Security Considerations\n\n- Access tokens are transmitted in the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` request header, which keeps them out of the request line and so out of a URL-based access log. They are not hidden from logging in general: an ingress or proxy that captures request headers records them, as it records an `Authorization` header, so header capture must redact `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` too.\n- The server answers with the `hal.v1` marker, so the token is never written into the 101 response headers or held as the connected socket's `protocol` property. An offer without the marker is answered with no subprotocol, so no offered value is ever echoed.\n- No offered subprotocol value is written to the engine's own log at any level. Every place a credential exists during a connection - request headers, the socket's and the session's `authHeaders`, and the tool context - is listed in [the subprotocol marker spec](../hal-engine-subprotocol-marker/spec.md#where-a-credential-exists).\n- Message content is validated at the server boundary. Content exceeding 10,000 characters is rejected.\n- The server validates all incoming messages against known types. Unrecognized types receive an `INVALID_MESSAGE` error.\n\n## 13. Source Files\n\n| Concern                  | File                                              |\n| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |\n| Shared entry types       | `src/types/session.ts`                            |\n| Backend message types    | `src/types/messages.ts`                           |\n| Backend sender helpers   | `src/transport/ws/sender.ts`                      |\n| Message validation       | `src/transport/ws/validation.ts`                  |\n| Message handling         | `src/transport/ws/messageHandler.ts`              |\n| Connection handler       | `src/transport/ws/connectionHandler.ts`           |\n","numLines":658,"startLine":1,"totalLines":658}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_eaf9a3408f6a49efbbfc4bea","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

a miss, a store failure and a not-yours all read as no resume.\nexport async function resumableSession(\n  store: SessionStore,\n  requester: Requester,\n  options?: SessionResumeOptions\n): Promise<ResumeOutcome> {\n  const found = await storedSession(store, requester, options);\n  if (found === undefined) return {};\n  if (found.status === 'active' && isOwnedBy(found, requester)) return {session: found.session};\n  // The latest-session default names no id, so there is no failure to report.\n  if (requester.requestedSessionId === undefined) return {};\n  return {failure: failureOf(found, requester)};\n}\n\nasync function storedSession(\n  store: SessionStore,\n  requester: Requester,\n  options: SessionResumeOptions | undefined\n): Promise<SessionLookup | undefined> {\n  try {\n    return await lookUp(store, requester, options);\n  } catch (error) {\n    const reason = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);\n    log.error('ws', 'session lookup failed', {userId: requester.userId, error: reason});\n    return {status: 'missing'};\n  }\n}\n\n// A named id first; with none, the user's latest session, unless resume asks for none or the client asked for a new one.\nasync function lookUp(\n  store: SessionStore,\n  {requestedSessionId, startNewSession, userId}: Requester,\n  options: SessionResumeOptions | undefined\n): Promise<SessionLookup | undefined> {\n  if (requestedSessionId !== undefined) return named(store, requestedSessionId);\n  if (!options?.enabled || !options.latest || startNewSession) return undefined;\n  return asLookup(await store.latestFor?.(userId));\n}\n\n// One read per attempt: the store's lookup when it has one, else its get, which can only tell active from missing.\nasync function named(store: SessionStore, sessionId: string): Promise<SessionLookup> {\n  if (store.lookup) return store.lookup(sessionId);\n  return asLookup(await store.get(sessionId));\n}\n\nfunction asLookup(session: ChatSession | undefined): SessionLookup {\n  return session === undefined ? {status: 'missing'} : {status: 'active', session};\n}\n\n// `expired` tells the owner their session aged out; {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_f7805f02c2e94ba1a7d645a6","type":"tool_result","content":"128:## Spec Test Links\n129-\n130-Statements in `specs/*/spec.md` cite their validating test in a trailing\n131-parenthetical at the end of the statement, where a list item counts as one\n132-statement and a paragraph counts per sentence. Tests live beside their source\n133-in this repo, so the path points into `src/`:\n134-\n135-```markdown\n136-- All entries within a single assistant response are committed before the next\n137-  user message is processed\n138-  ([validated by: commits every entry before the next user message](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L42)).\n139-```\n140-\n141-The citation carries the test's **name** as well as its line. The name is what the\n142-author cited; the line is a derived pointer, and it goes stale on its own - adding\n143-an import above a suite moves every test below it, and the citation lands on a\n144-different, still-valid declaration without anything noticing. `npm run spec:names`\n145-holds each citation to the test it names, and `npm run spec:names:fix` repoints the\n146-line from the name. The `#Lnn` stays because the lint rule and the coverage job\n147-both index by it; a citation without one marks the whole file covered rather than\n148-one test.\n149-\n150-A citation counts as coverage only where it is trailing, and a test link placed\n151-anywhere else in the statement is a misplaced citation rather than a weaker one.\n152-Upstream `check:spec-links` reports it and exits 1, and the coverage job that\n153-consumes these specs records nothing for it - so a spec can read as fully cited while its coverage is\n154-zero. A mid-statement link to something that is not a test file - a script, a\n155-doc, another spec - is ordinary prose, is never reported, and was never coverage\n156-to begin with. A misplaced citation is fixed by moving it to the end of its\n157-statement, never by deleting it.\n158-\n159-In a test file the `#Lnn` anchor must land on the `it(`, `test(` or `describe(`\n160-declaration itself - not a blank line, not one holding only closing punctuation,\n161-and not a line inside the test body. A citation onto an `expect` renders and\n162-resolves like any other, and proves nothing: no reader can turn that line back\n163-into the name of a case. `scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs` reports all four as\n164-`rotten` and exits 1 in both modes. A citation into a file that is not a test -\n165-a workflow, a config, `package.json` - has no declaration to land on and is held\n166-only to existing and carrying content.\n167-\n168-What no gate can catch is an anchor aimed at the wrong declaration: a real but\n169-unintended `it(` passes every check. The tell is that the test the statement\n170-meant to cite goes on reading as uncited in the `require-spec-link` backlog.\n171-\n172-Anchors drift silently whenever a cited file gains or loses lines above them, so\n173-after editing any cited file re-run `node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs`","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"45b3f278-4b8a-4893-8375-456473c69c1e","uuid":"81773571-f9bc-48d2-8182-19b35ec26cbf","timestamp":"2026-11-04T13:08:01.474Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"128:## Spec Test Links\n129-\n130-Statements in `specs/*/spec.md` cite their validating test in a trailing\n131-parenthetical at the end of the statement, where a list item counts as one\n132-statement and a paragraph counts per sentence. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_4a9c0cbf777b4784a38994db","type":"tool_result","content":"and the changelog check.\n\nTwo further CI jobs are worth running locally before a release or a change that\ntouches packaging: `npm run check:build-chain` (audit and action pins) and\n`npm run smoke` (packs the tarball and installs it outside this tree).\n\n## Spec Header Table\n\nEvery `specs/*/spec.md` opens with its title, then a two-column header table,\nand carries a lead paragraph of prose before its first `##` section:\n\n```markdown\n# <spec title>\n\n| Field  | Value                  |\n| ------ | ---------------------- |\n| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#<n> |\n| Status | Draft                  |\n\n<lead paragraph>\n```\n\nThe lead paragraph does not have to sit immediately after the table: a spec\ncarrying a metadata block of its own may place that block between the two. What\nthe convention requires is that prose, rather than a section heading, follows\nthe header material, and that the prose runs to at least 40 characters -\nanything shorter is reported as no lead paragraph at all.\n\n`Issue` names the issue the spec was written against, or `n/a` for the specs\nthat predate this convention.\n\n`Status` is one of `Draft`, `In Progress` or `Shipped`. It is not a mood, and\nit is not a claim about how finished the feature is: it is the spec's own\ntest-citation coverage. No testable statement cited is `Draft`, some cited is\n`In Progress`, all cited is `Shipped`. A spec describing shipped, working\nbehaviour still reads `Draft` until its statements cite the tests that\nvalidate them.\n\nA spec that should no longer be graded takes a terminal value instead. The\nparser buckets roughly sixteen labels into five buckets, and the two terminal\nones skip the coverage check whatever the citation count:\n\n| Written into the spec                                            | Bucket                       |\n| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |\n| `Draft`                                                          | `draft`                      |\n| `In Progress`, `In Review`, `Planning`, `WIP`, `Proposed`        | `in-progress`                |\n| `Shipped`, `Implemented`, `Complete`, `Accepted`, `Done`, `Live` | `shipped`                    |\n| `Retired`, `Superseded`, `Removed`, `Deprecated`, `Obsolete`     | `retired` - skips the check  |\n| `Rejected`, `Abandoned`                                          | `rejected` - skips the check |\n\nPrefer the canonical `Draft` / `In Progress` / `Shipped` for a live spec; reach\nfor `Retired` or `Rejected` rather than leaving a superseded spec to claim a\ncoverage tier it will never earn.\n\nADRs do not carry this table. They declare their state as YAML frontmatter\n`status:` instead - `accepted` for a decision the code implements, `proposed`\nfor one it does not. That field does mean maturity, which the spec `Status` row\nexplicitly does not. The difference is deliberate: ADRs are exempt from the\ncoverage tier, because asking a decision record to cite a test for every\nstatement it makes is the wrong ask of a decision record.\n\n`.specify/spec.md` is exempt from this section. What\nthe convention requires is that prose, rather than a section heading, follows\nthe header material, and that the prose runs to at least 40 characters -\nanything shorter is reported as no lead paragraph at all.\n\n`Issue` names the issue the spec was written against, or `n/a` for the specs\nthat predate this convention.\n\n`Status` is one of `Draft`, `In Progress` or `Shipped`.
